summary: Nikolai Anderson (1845–1905) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu (1865–1875) under Leo Meyer. He served as Oberlehrer für alte Sprachen at Minsk Gymnasium (1872–1894) and Eo. Professor of Finno-Ugric at Kazan State University (1894–1905).

Nikolai Maksimovich Goldberg (1891–1961) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University (1910–1912) and held posts at the Institute of History of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR (1938) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1943).

Nikolai Solmsdorf is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, also studying under Alexander von Rospatt, and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nikolai Trubetzkoy (1890–1938) was a linguist who studied at Moscow State University under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Southern Federal University, Sofia University, and the University of Vienna.

Nikolaj Dmitrievič Andreev (1920–1997) was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He worked at the National Library of Russia, Leningrad State University's Experimental Laboratory of Machine Translation, and the Institute for Linguistic Studies.

Nikolaus Delius (1813–1888) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Bonn under Franz Bopp, Christian Lassen, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel, later serving as Professor of English at Bonn (1855–1880).

Nikolay Astakhaev worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Buryat State University (2005–2008) and later worked as a system administrator at the Irkutsk Institute of Educators Training (2012–2015) and at Yandex's Novosibirsk office (2015).

Nikolay Ivanovich Korolev (1928–1995) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Institute of Asian and African Studies at Moscow State University (~1953–1958) and served as a research scholar at the Institute of Oriental Studies from 1958.

Nils Holmer (1904–1994) was a linguist who studied at Lund University and Charles University. He served as Privatdozent of Celtic and Indo-European at Uppsala University in 1941 and as Professor of Linguistics at Lund University from 1949 to 1969.

Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg (1855–1926) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lund University (fil.kand. 1880, Ph.D. ~1888). He taught at Lunds privata elementarskola and served as Privatdozent and Professor of Sanskrit at Lund University.

Nils Simonsson (1920–1994) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. Educated at Uppsala and Oslo, he studied under Helmer Smith, Louis Renou, Marcelle Lalou, and Georg Morgenstierne. He served as Professor at the University of Oslo and later at Uppsala University.
Nima Repper is an Indology scholar who is attested in 2026 as having studied at and held the post of Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Nimethri Gunasekara works in Buddhist studies and psychology. She served as a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Kelaniya in 2024 and is attested in 2026 at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies as a psychologist and visiting lecturer.

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her doctoral studies under Alexis Sanderson. She has held posts at the University of Groningen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna.

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Oxford and Yale. He served as Professor at the University of Birmingham, Lancaster University, and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Nira Wickramasinghe (born 1964) is a historian and Indologist. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and the University of Oxford, and held posts as Professor at the University of Colombo (1990–2009) and Chair of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University (2010).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop. He worked at the Nepal Research Centre, Leiden University, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale," and joined Ashoka University in 2023.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Calcutta, Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge under Edward James Rapson. He lectured at Calcutta and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1948–1950).

Nirbhay N. Singh is a scholar of religious studies and psychiatry. He held posts as Clinical Professor at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018), Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies.
Nirmal C. Sinha served as Editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology, attested in 1978 and 1988.
